key_insight: Use reliable visual features to guide prompt learning so the learned prompts are robust to label noise. VisPrompt fuses cross-modal signals to prevent noisy labels from corrupting text prompt optimization.
problem_solved: Prompt tuning for vision-language models is highly sensitive to noisy training labels; this paper addresses how to make prompt learning robust when labels are corrupted or unreliable.
method: Introduce a lightweight vision-guided prompt learning framework that conditions prompt updates on visual features rather than relying solely on noisy labels.
Use cross-modal guidance (e.g., attention/affinity between image features and prompt tokens) to align prompt optimization with image semantics and reduce label-noise influence.
Design parameter-efficient modules and training objectives that regularize prompts with visual context, maintaining robustness without heavy extra modeling cost.
impact: Makes prompt learning practical on real-world datasets where labels are noisy, improving reliability of vision-language systems with minimal extra parameters—beneficial for deployment and few-shot learning scenarios.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: image encoder -> visual-guidance module -> prompt tokens -> text encoder/classifier (showing cross-modal links)
Before vs. after bar chart: prompt-only tuning accuracy under increasing label noise vs. VisPrompt robustness
Attention/heatmap visualization: how visual features influence specific prompt tokens (illustrating mitigation of noisy-label effects)
Training flowchart: noisy labels + visual guidance -> contrastive/regularized prompt update -> robust classifier
paper_title: Seeing is Believing: Robust Vision-Guided Cross-Modal Prompt Learning under Label Noise
paper_authors: Zibin Geng, Xuefeng Jiang, Jia Li, Zheng Li, Tian Wen
